principle: Compared figures are each paper's best reported model on the shared metric (best against best). Where the two evaluation sets have different class mixes, the pair is judged on the prevalence-free figures both papers support (AUC where both print it, otherwise balanced accuracy from printed class-wise rates). Raw accuracy is reported alongside. SEs follow the brief: printed 95% CI -> (upper - lower)/3.92; otherwise binomial or Hanley-McNeil on subject-level n; a printed +/- fold spread is not used as an SE.

results.compared: AD vs MCI from MRI in ADNI, AUC of each paper's best model: P-152 Gaussian-kernel SVM on superficial-white-matter DTI features (Table 3, MCI-AD row) against P-301 ROI-3DViT-DBN ensemble on T1 regional volumes (Table 3, DBN row). No matched figure exists (P-152 has no T1 analysis, P-301 no diffusion analysis, neither reports the other's class balance).

a.se_source: No interval printed. Hanley-McNeil with 24 AD/24 MCI ('This method employed DTI data from 72 subjects: 24 subjects as HC, 24 subjects with MCI, and 24 subjects with AD'): Q1 = 0.93/1.07 = 0.869, Q2 = 2(0.8649)/1.93 = 0.896, SE = sqrt([0.0651 + 23(0.0043) + 23(0.0314)]/576) = 0.0392.

b.se_source: No interval and no validation n printed ('we divided the ADNI dataset into training and validation sets using an 80/20 split. All reported results reflect the model's performance on the validation set'). n derived as 20% of 117 AD + 247 MCI = about 72 (23 AD/49 MCI). Hanley-McNeil: Q1 = 0.6/1.4 = 0.429, Q2 = 0.72/1.6 = 0.450, SE = sqrt([0.24 + 22(0.069) + 48(0.090)]/1127) = 0.0734. At a validation n of 50 (16/34) SE = 0.0883.

results.one_sentence: On AD versus MCI from MRI in ADNI, P-152 (diffusion MRI, 24 AD/24 MCI, 5-fold CV after feature selection) reports AUC 0.93 and P-301 (T1 MRI, 80/20 split of 364 AD+MCI scans) reports AUROC 0.60, a gap beyond combined uncertainty (z = 3.97; balanced accuracy 0.835 against 0.60, z = 3.43), although the raw accuracies (83.3% and 74%) do not differ beyond uncertainty (z = 1.25); the differences in MRI features, sample size and validation, class balance, MCI composition and architecture are candidate explanations, none shown to be sufficient.
results.reason: z = |0.93 - 0.60| / sqrt(0.0392^2 + 0.0734^2) = 0.33/0.0832 = 3.97; at a derived validation n of 60 it is 3.68 and at 50 it is 3.42, so the result does not hinge on the derived n. P-301's AUROC equals the balanced accuracy implied by its own accuracy 0.74, kappa 0.25 and a 32% AD share (pe = 0.653, predicted-AD share 0.074, sensitivity 0.21, specificity 0.99), so it appears to be a hard-label value; the like-for-like balanced-accuracy test also passes: P-152 (0.807 + 0.863)/2 = 0.835, SE 0.5 x sqrt(0.807 x 0.193/24 + 0.863 x 0.137/24) = 0.0534, against 0.60, SE 0.5 x sqrt(0.21 x 0.79/23 + 0.99 x 0.01/49) = 0.0431, z = 0.235/0.0686 = 3.43. The prevalence-dependent figures do not separate the papers: raw accuracy 40/48 = 0.833 (SE 0.0538) against 0.74 (SE 0.0517 at n = 72) gives z = 1.25, and P-152's sensitivity and specificity reweighted to P-301's 32% AD share give 0.845 (SE 0.0542), z = 1.40 against 0.74, because P-301's classifier calls about 93% of a 68%-MCI set MCI. On the prevalence-free figures the gap is beyond combined uncertainty. Source checks: P-301's Table 3 caption follows the DBN 0.74/0.60/0.69/0.25 block and matches its text ('In the AD vs. MCI task, the proposed approach achieved an accuracy of 74% and an AUROC of 60%'); P-152's Table 3 MCI-AD row reads 83.3/80.7/86.3/.93. Neither compared figure reaches 0.97 (P-152's AD vs HC 0.99 is not compared). The record's own pairing (P-152 AD vs HC 95.8% against P-301 AD vs MCI 0.74) misreads the contrasts and is set aside under condition 6. This pair came through the reader+skeptic route; the round-1 skeptic (challenge_skeptic_5) found no failed condition, and the full skeptic check was not repeated here. The qualification rests on a derived validation n for P-301 and on P-152's small-sample CV with FCBF feature selection run before the folds and the best of several kernels reported, which are recorded as candidate explanations, not shown to be sufficient.
candidate_explanations: Features within the MRI channel: diffusion-tensor, tractography and connectivity features of the superficial white matter (P-152: 'classify patients with AD and MCI and healthy control (HC) subjects based on the diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) features in the superficial white matter (SWM)') against T1 regional volumes through 138 per-ROI 3D vision transformers (P-301).

Sample size and validation: 48 subjects per contrast with FCBF feature selection before an internal 5-fold CV and the best kernel reported (P-152: 'After feature selection, we performed an internal 5-fold cross-validation for the training data'; 'we show the Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and the area under the curve (AUC) for the best kernel in each classification') against a single 80/20 split of 364 AD+MCI scans (P-301).
Class balance and operating point: balanced 24/24 in P-152 against 117 AD/247 MCI in P-301, where the derived AD sensitivity is about 0.21 and the AUROC appears to be computed from hard labels.

MCI composition: 140 of P-301's 247 amnestic MCI progress within 24 months ('further classified as 107 with stable MCI (sMCI) and 140 with progressive MCI (pMCI) based on their disease development over 24 months'); P-152 does not report its MCI composition.
Cohort subset: ADNI2 DTI participants (P-152: 'were recruited from the ADNI2 project') against a baseline ADNI T1 dataset labelled by two-year change in diagnosis (P-301).

Architecture: kernel SVM on selected features against a deep-belief-network ensemble over 138 ROI vision transformers (P-301: 'we propose the ROI-3DViT-DBN ensemble model for the early prediction of AD').

results.compared: MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI MCI, AUC of each paper's best model: P-178 9-feature random forest (Table 4) against P-183 ENS on neuropsychological plus T2-map imaging features (Table 4, the best AUC in that table). No matched figure exists (P-178 has no 2-year horizon, no 70-80 subset and no T2 features; P-183 has no early-MCI or eventual-conversion subset).

a.se_source: No interval printed. Hanley-McNeil on subject-level n: 95 test patients ('the remaining 25% (95 patients) used for validation testing'), about 12 converters (49 of 383 patients converted) and 83 non-converters: Q1 = 0.96/1.04 = 0.923, Q2 = 2(0.9216)/1.96 = 0.940, SE = sqrt([0.0384 + 11(0.0015) + 82(0.0188)]/996) = 0.0400. At visit level (about 45/402) SE = 0.0206.

results.one_sentence: For MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI, P-178 reports AUC 0.96 (early MCI, clinical scales plus hippocampal and ventricular volume, visit-level 95-patient test) and P-183 reports at best AUC 0.824 (95% CI 0.681-0.968; 40 patients, T2-map features plus neuropsychology), a difference not beyond combined uncertainty (z = 1.63), and P-178's higher accuracy (93.6% against 77.5%) comes from a test set that is 90% non-converters.
results.reason: z = |0.96 - 0.824| / sqrt(0.0400^2 + 0.0732^2) = 0.136/0.0834 = 1.63. The test fails however P-178's n is taken: with visit-level n z = 1.79, and even with P-178's SE set to zero z = 0.136/0.0732 = 1.86. The advocate (challenge_advocate_7) qualified the pair on AUC by the one-way test (0.824 below P-178's derived 0.882) and by z = 2.39 against P-183's RF (0.770, SE 0.0686); P-183's other models give z = 2.03 (LASSO 0.773), 2.29 (BSWiMS 0.732), 2.49 (KNN 0.721) and 2.67 (SVM 0.742). Comparing P-178's best model with a weaker P-183 model is not the neutral comparison: P-183 designates no primary model, and against its best AUC the gap is within combined uncertainty. Skeptic check of conditions 1 to 6: (1) holds, both predict conversion in ADNI Alzheimer's-spectrum MCI from cognitive scores plus MRI measures, with population subset, horizon and features differing as allowed; (2) holds, AUC with AUC; (3) holds on AUC (on accuracy it fails: P-178's printed precision 0.952 and recall 0.978, with the 90% non-converter test share fixed by its SVC row, give sensitivity 0.556 and specificity 0.978, 0.788 at P-183's 45% converters against 0.775, and balanced accuracy 0.767 against 0.770-0.777; raw accuracy 0.936 against 0.775 gives z = 2.15 only through that class mix); (4) fails under the uniform test; (5) holds, 0.96 and 0.936 are below 0.97 on 383 patients; (6) the record's 'P-183: Acc 72.7' is a misread (0.727 is P-183's neuropsychology-only LASSO AUC: 'The machine learning technique with the best results was LASSO, with an accuracy of 0.675 and an ROC AUC of 0.727'), and the pair is judged on P-183's printed Table 4. The first-pass reader's verdict (borderline, not reported on accuracy) is upheld and the advocate's overturn is not.
candidate_explanations: Class prevalence (accuracy only): P-178's test set is about 90% non-converters and P-183's is 45% converters; P-178's own figures show this is enough to explain the accuracy gap, but it does not bear on AUC (P-178: 'One observation when observing our SVC model is that it struggled to predict the negative class (conversion to AD) and predominantly chose the majority class').

Evaluation unit and split: P-178 scores exam visits, including converter visits close to conversion, and its Table 1 splits oversampled records 1206/402 per class, which reads as a record-level split, although its text describes a patient-level 288/95 split (Table 1: 'Record# after Oversampling 1608 1608 Training Data 1206 1206 Testing Data 402 402').

Feature group chosen on test accuracy (P-178: 'While initially, using all 13-features seemed to provide the highest accuracy at 91.6%, we found that by removing the RAVLT features, our accuracy rose to 93.6% in the 9-feature group').

Population and horizon: early-MCI patients labelled by last-visit diagnosis (eventual conversion, 5-7 years) against MCI aged 70-80 progressing at 2 years or stable for at least 5 years (P-183: 'the 18 subjects who had their first AD diagnosis 2 years after their baseline visit were regarded as progressers (MCIp), while the 22 subjects who never had an AD diagnosis and participated in the study for at least 5 years were labeled as stable (MCIs)').

Features: diagnosis-related scales (ADAS13, ADAS11, FAQ, MMSE) with hippocampal and ventricular volume, APOE4 and demographics (P-178) against eight neuropsychological scores with T2-map signal and texture features (P-183).
Sample size: 40 subjects in P-183, which makes its intervals wide (P-183: 'the inclusion criteria forced us to work with a small population').

results.compared: MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI MCI, held-out accuracy of each paper's best model: P-178 9-feature random forest (Table 4) against P-212 ensemble on its 139-subject test set ('the most accurate model (i.e. the ensemble model)'). No figure is printed under the other paper's condition (every P-178 model includes ADAS, MMSE and FAQ; P-212 has none with them and no early-MCI subgroup). P-212 reports no AUC.

a.se_source: No interval printed. Binomial on subject-level n = 95 test patients ('with 95 patients reserved for testing'): sqrt(0.936 x 0.064/95) = 0.0251.

b.se_source: No interval printed. 95/139 correct ('The ensemble algorithm misclassified 20/74 sMCI subjects as converters and 24/65 cAD subjects as stable'): sqrt(0.683 x 0.317/139) = 0.0395. (RF: 92/139 = 0.662, SE 0.0401.)

results.one_sentence: For MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI, P-178 reports 93.6% accuracy and P-212 68.3% on held-out data, but P-178's test set is 90% non-converters, and at P-212's class mix P-178's own class-wise figures give about 78% (balanced accuracy 0.77 against 0.68), a difference not beyond combined uncertainty (z = 1.24; 1.06 for balanced accuracy).
results.reason: Raw z = |0.936 - 0.683| / sqrt(0.0251^2 + 0.0395^2) = 0.253/0.0468 = 5.40 (5.79 against P-212's RF). The raw figures are not the same quantity, because the class mixes differ: P-178's SVC row ('Support Vector 9-Features 0.900 0.900 1 0.948 0.54') fixes its test set at 90% non-converters, so its accuracy of 0.936 sits 0.036 above its no-information rate, against 47% converters in P-212. P-178's printed precision 0.952 and recall 0.978 then give converter sensitivity 0.556 and specificity 0.978. At P-212's 65/139 = 46.8% converters that is 0.468(0.556) + 0.532(0.978) = 0.781, SE sqrt(0.468^2 x 0.556 x 0.444/12 + 0.532^2 x 0.978 x 0.022/83) = 0.0676 (about 12 converters and 83 non-converters among the 95 test patients), against 0.683: z = 0.098/sqrt(0.0676^2 + 0.0395^2) = 1.24 (1.51 against the RF's 0.662). Balanced accuracy, 0.767 (SE 0.0722) against the ensemble's (0.631 + 0.730)/2 = 0.680 (SE 0.0395), gives z = 1.06 (1.31 against the RF's 0.659). P-178's own printed figures therefore show that the class mix of its test set is enough to bring the gap inside combined uncertainty, which under the brief is a paper showing an explanation to be sufficient: condition 3 fails. The first pass and the round-1 skeptic (challenge_skeptic_6) qualified the pair because the adjusted 0.781 lies outside P-212's held-out interval (upper bound 0.755), one way only; that is the one-way test the verification round replaces. Two caveats for the operator: (a) per class, sensitivity agrees (0.556 against 0.631, z = 0.48) while specificity does not (0.978 against 0.730, z = 4.59), but specificity alone depends on the threshold and is not a like-for-like performance figure; (b) with visit-level n (about 45 converter visits) the balanced-accuracy z would be 1.60-1.97, but the brief requires subject-level n and visits within a patient are not independent. Conditions 1, 2, 5 and 6 hold as the first pass found. This pair came through the reader+skeptic route, so the full skeptic check was not repeated.
candidate_explanations: Class prevalence and chance level: P-178's test set is about 90% non-converters, P-212's 47% converters; P-178's own figures show this brings the gap inside combined uncertainty (Table 4 SVC: 'Support Vector 9-Features 0.900 0.900 1 0.948 0.54').

Diagnosis-defining scales as predictors: P-178 uses 'four neuropsychological scale scores (ADAS13, ADAS11, FAQ, MMSE)'; P-212 excludes them because 'scores from the neuropsychological tests used to define "ground truth" labels (i.e. stable or converters) were also included as predictors, which potentially could lead to inflated predictive performance due to circularity'.

Population: early MCI only (P-178: 'Early Mild Cognitive Impairment (EMCI) patients were eligible for our study as long as they had follow-up appointments for greater than a year') against all ADNI MCI with at least three visits and three MRIs (P-212).

Evaluation unit and oversampling: visit-level records with random minority oversampling, and a Table 1 testing row (402/402) inconsistent with Table 4 (P-178: 'This allows for the model to be trained against 2412 exam visits (1206 per class) rather than only the 1354 from the original data set train/test split'), against one record per subject in P-212.
Feature group chosen on test accuracy (P-178: 'by removing the RAVLT features, our accuracy rose to 93.6% in the 9-feature group').

Validation: a single random 95-patient split against a stratified 139-subject held-out set after 50-fold CV, where P-212's own CV-to-test drop shows the split variance (P-212: 'Our top performing RF classification had an average accuracy of 74.6% (mean across 50 cross-validation folds). When the model was evaluated on our unseen test set, the overall classification accuracy was 66.2%').
Overlapping ADNI participants (ADNI-1/GO/2 in both), so the two samples are not fully independent.

results.compared: Stable against progressive MCI in ADNI from baseline structural MRI, AUC of each paper's reported model: P-185 linear SVM on the subspace biomarker (69.37%/0.6951) against P-41 heterogeneous EfficientNet + ConvNeXt + DenseNet ensemble with attention and MHA head (91.77%/0.9287). No matched figure exists (P-41 has no pMCI-only or ROI-feature model; P-185 no slice-based model).

b.se_source: No interval printed. Hanley-McNeil with 126 pMCI/95 sMCI ('the 221 MCI subjects contain 126 pMCI and 95 sMCI subjects'; 10-fold CV repeated 20 times): Q1 = 0.6951/1.3049 = 0.533, Q2 = 2(0.4832)/1.6951 = 0.570, SE = sqrt([0.2119 + 125(0.0495) + 94(0.0869)]/11970) = 0.0349.

results.one_sentence: For stable against progressive MCI from baseline structural MRI in ADNI, P-41 reports AUC 0.929 (accuracy 91.8%) on a 30-subject test and P-185 AUC 0.695 (accuracy 69.4%) on 221 subjects (z = 3.80), but P-41's own configurations without its attention module and ensemble score AUC 0.80-0.85 on the same test subjects, which does not differ from P-185 beyond combined uncertainty (z 1.14-1.85), so P-41's own ablation places the gap in architecture choices made on its test set.
results.reason: Headline z = |0.9287 - 0.6951| / sqrt(0.0505^2 + 0.0349^2) = 0.2336/0.0614 = 3.80; on accuracy, 0.9177 (SE 0.0502, n = 30) against 0.6937 (SE 0.0310, n = 221) gives 3.80, and at the 0.881 implied by P-41's own sensitivity and specificity z = 2.81. Skeptic check of conditions 1 to 6: (1) holds, sMCI vs pMCI in ADNI from baseline sMRI; the 15 AD patients added to P-41's positive class are a label-definition difference the rule allows; (2) holds; (4) holds on the headline figures; (5) holds, 0.929 and 0.918 are below 0.97; (6) holds, 'P-41: Acc 91' is what P-41 prints. Condition 3 fails. The advocate (challenge_advocate_7) overturned the reader's condition-3 finding by showing that P-41's Experiment-1 configurations without attention lie outside P-185's intervals, which is the one-way test, partly on printed accuracies that exceed both their own sensitivity and specificity, impossible on a 15/15 test. Under the uniform test, on the same 30 test subjects, P-41's configurations without attention do not differ from P-185 beyond combined uncertainty on AUC: ConvNext+LSTM coronal 0.8266 (Hanley-McNeil SE 0.0774) z = 0.1315/0.0849 = 1.55; DenseNet+LSTM axial 0.8454 (SE 0.0735) z = 1.85 (0.8054 in Table 2, z = 1.25); EfficientNet+MHA sagittal 0.7979 (SE 0.0828) z = 1.14. Nor do the accuracies their sensitivity and specificity imply (0.787, 0.801, 0.736; z = 1.15, 1.35, 0.49); the printed 83.94% and 85.78% would give 1.97 and 2.31 but cannot be right. The gap passes the test only once attention is added to the best single model (EfficientNet+MHA sagittal with attention, AUC 0.8879, SE 0.0631, z = 2.68; ConvNext coronal with attention 0.8166, z = 1.40) and in the ensemble (z = 3.80). All of these were configurations scored and chosen on the same 30 test subjects. So P-41's own ablation shows that the plain version of its method is within uncertainty of P-185 and that the architecture additions carry the result beyond it. That is the C-147/C-155/C-117 convention, which the advocate itself accepted, and under it condition 3 fails. The reader's verdict stands. If the operator does not count a within-paper ablation under condition 3, the headline figures pass the test (z = 3.80).
candidate_explanations: Architecture and representation: an attention-augmented, multi-plane CNN ensemble on 132 2D slices per plane against a linear SVM on FreeSurfer regional thickness and volume in a learned subspace. P-41's ablation shows its configurations without attention and ensembling are within uncertainty of P-185 (P-41: 'In the case of ConvNext+LSTM with coronal plane, the model without attention achieved an accuracy of 83.94% +/-5.32, sensitivity of 77.34% +/-5.34, specificity of 79.96% +/-4.31, and an AUC of 82.66% +/-3.28').

Configuration selection on the test set: many backbone, head and plane combinations are all scored on the same 30 test subjects and the best are carried forward (P-41: 'all results reported in this study were based on the test set').

Label definition: 15 patients with established AD are added to P-41's positive class (P-41: 'Furthermore, we added 15 patients with AD to the pMCI group to help the model learn both the progressive and fully diseased brain patterns simultaneously').

Horizon: conversion within 3 years (P-185: 'According to whether the MCI subjects will convert to AD or not within a given time period (i.e., 3 years)') against conversion between M18 and M48 with stability to M48 (P-41).

Test size and validation: a single 15 + 15 subject test set (P-41, Table 1) against 20 repetitions of 10-fold CV on 221 MCI (P-185: 'repeated 10-fold cross-validation 20 times to report the average results for each method').
Field strength and ADNI phase: 1.5 T (P-185: 'We use baseline MRI scans (1.5 T, 1:25 mm x 1:25 mm in-plane spatial resolution, 1.2 mm thick slices)') against 3 T MPRAGE from ADNI 2 (P-41).

Reporting reliability: P-41's printed accuracies exceed both its sensitivity and its specificity throughout its tables (P-41: 'an accuracy of 91.77% +/-3.14, sensitivity of 87.69% +/-3.24, specificity of 88.53% +/-3.53, and an impressive AUC of 92.87% +/-3.58').
